Generation of a neutral partition given parameter \(\theta\) using Hoppe's urn

Source: R/generation.R
generate_hoppe_urn0.Rd

generate_hoppe_urn0() creates a rank-abundance distribution based on Hoppe's urn scheme for a given parameter \(\theta\) and sample size J. The process starts at zero species, corresponding to the single black ball with weight \(\theta\). If the black ball is picked, a new class is created, else the picked colored ball is duplicated (its abundance increases by one unit).

This is an exact simulation of the urn, but it does not loop over the individuals: the genealogy of the J individuals is resolved in a handful of vectorised passes, and the random numbers come from the fast dqrng generator. Memory use is proportional to J, so it is meant for J up to a few hundred million; for larger samples use generate_hoppe_urn().

Usage

generate_hoppe_urn0(theta, J, seed = NULL)

Arguments

theta

parameter \(\theta\), a positive real value

J

number of individuals, a whole number

seed

optional integer; if given, the dqrng generator is seeded with it (this changes the state of the dqrng generator for the whole session)

Value

generate_hoppe_urn0() returns the species abundances, an integer vector sorted in decreasing order and summing to J.

Reproducibility

generate_hoppe_urn0() draws its random numbers from dqrng, which has its own random number stream: set.seed() has no effect on it. Use the seed argument instead. generate_hoppe_urn() and generate_pitman_urn() use R's standard generator and follow set.seed().

See also

generate_hoppe_urn() for a faster approach on very large samples

Examples

generate_hoppe_urn0(11.3, 234373, seed = 1)
#>   [1] 60996 24243 21303 13817 13297  9833  7847  7082  7008  6435  5523  5501
#>  [13]  5265  3799  3324  3117  3002  2915  2772  2584  2480  2240  1865  1816
#>  [25]  1747  1708  1383  1277  1032   918   845   793   744   668   562   447
#>  [37]   417   259   242   240   231   228   212   206   186   173   152   144
#>  [49]   130   117   109   105   102   102    92    79    70    63    61    57
#>  [61]    53    42    36    29    27    26    21    18    16    11    11    10
#>  [73]    10     9     8     8     6     6     6     5     5     4     3     3
